name: Pixel Bit Plane
description: Analyzes bit plane patterns for hidden artifacts
algorithm: Pixel Bit Plane — Pixel-Level Spatial Analysis
mechanism:
This method analyzes pixel bit planes for image forensic analysis following the steganalysis framework of Fridrich & Kodovsky (2012):

1. **Bit Plane Decomposition**: Each pixel value is decomposed into its constituent bit planes (8 bit planes for 8-bit images). Each bit plane is a binary image representing one bit position across all pixels. Higher bit planes carry structural information; lower bit planes carry fine detail and noise.

2. **Bit Plane Statistics**: Statistical properties of each bit plane are analyzed — randomness (entropy), spatial correlation, and pattern regularity. In natural images, lower bit planes approach random binary noise while higher bit planes show image structure. AI-generated images may show different bit plane statistics — especially in lower planes where the generator's quantization produces non-random patterns.

3. **Bit Plane Correlation Analysis**: The correlation between adjacent bit planes is measured. Natural camera images show specific inter-plane correlation patterns arising from the sensor's analog-to-digital conversion. AI-generated pixels don't arise from A/D conversion and may show different inter-plane correlations.

4. **LSB Plane Analysis**: The least significant bit (LSB) plane receives special attention. In natural images, the LSB plane appears quasi-random. AI generators, depending on their output quantization method, may produce LSB planes with: residual patterns, reduced entropy, or spatial correlations that reveal the generation process.

5. **Multi-Plane Feature Scoring**: Features from all bit planes are combined into a forensic score. The score captures bit plane entropy ratios, inter-plane correlation anomalies, and spatial regularity in individual planes.
parameters:
Analysis type: pixel
Media: image
Input: Raw pixel data / image file
Output: Confidence score (0-100)
Processing: Client-side Canvas API
Color spaces: RGB, Grayscale as applicable
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-90% standalone accuracy. Performance is highest on uncompressed images and may decrease with heavy JPEG compression or social media re-encoding.
source: Digital image forensics research. Based on signal processing and computational photography principles.
useCase: Detection of AI-generated or manipulated images through pixel bit plane analysis. This method identifies patterns and artifacts that are characteristic of AI generation, contributing to a comprehensive image forensic analysis.
strengths:
• Fast client-side processing using Canvas API
• Effective at detecting specific AI generation artifacts
• Works with common image formats (JPEG, PNG, WebP)
• Can be combined with complementary analysis methods
• Based on established image forensics research
limitations:
• Performance may vary with image compression level
• Social media re-encoding can affect accuracy
• Best used in combination with other forensic methods
• May produce false positives on heavily processed authentic images
• Effectiveness depends on the AI generation model used

references.title: Fridrich, J. & Kodovsky, J. (2012). Rich Models for Steganalysis of Digital Images. IEEE TIFS.
Gonzalez, R.C. & Woods, R.E. (2018). Digital Image Processing. 4th Edition. Pearson.
